tour.title: Project Overview
tour.description: StreamTube is a video sharing platform built as a monorepo with NestJS backend, Next.js frontend, PostgreSQL database, and Docker infrastructure. Start here to understand the project's purpose, architecture, and how to get started.

tour.title: Backend Entry Point
tour.description: The NestJS application bootstraps from main.ts, setting up the Express server, global pipes, Swagger documentation, and module imports. This is where the backend starts and wires together all NestJS modules.
tour.languageLesson: NestJS uses decorators (@Module, @Controller, @Injectable) to define module structure. The bootstrap function creates the app and listens on a configured port.

tour.title: Backend Architecture
tour.description: The app module is the root NestJS module that imports all feature modules (auth, users, channels, videos, comments). Each module encapsulates its own controllers, services, and entities following the single responsibility principle.

tour.title: Authentication System
tour.description: The auth module implements JWT-based authentication with refresh token rotation, password hashing via argon2, and email confirmation. It provides guards, strategies, and decorators for protecting routes.
tour.languageLesson: NestJS guards implement CanActivate to protect routes. JWT strategy validates tokens from the Authorization header. Refresh token rotation issues new tokens on each refresh for security.

tour.title: Data Layer
tour.description: TypeORM entities define the database schema for users, channels, and authentication tokens. The data source configures the PostgreSQL connection, and migrations manage schema evolution.
tour.languageLesson: TypeORM entities use decorators (@Entity, @Column, @ManyToOne) to map TypeScript classes to database tables. Migrations are version-controlled schema changes that can be applied and reverted.

tour.title: API Documentation
tour.description: OpenAPI/Swagger documentation is auto-generated from NestJS decorators. The openapi-export script produces a static spec file that the frontend uses for type-safe API client generation.

tour.title: Frontend Architecture
tour.description: The Next.js 16 frontend uses the App Router with React Server Components and a BFF (Backend-for-Frontend) pattern. Route Handlers in app/api/** proxy requests to the NestJS API, keeping the backend URL server-side.
tour.languageLesson: Next.js App Router uses file-system routing where folder structure defines routes. React Server Components render on the server, reducing client bundle size. Route Handlers act as API endpoints within the Next.js app.

tour.title: Frontend Auth Flow
tour.description: The auth pages implement login, registration, and password recovery using React Hook Form with Zod validation. MSW (Mock Service Worker) intercepts API calls during testing. The BFF pattern routes all API traffic through Next.js Route Handlers.

tour.title: UI Components
tour.description: The design system uses shadcn/ui components built on Radix UI primitives with Tailwind CSS v4. Components follow a composable pattern with variant-based styling via class-variance-authority.
tour.languageLesson: shadcn/ui is not a traditional component library — it copies component source code into your project for full control. Tailwind CSS v4 uses @theme inline for custom design tokens.

tour.title: Testing Strategy
tour.description: The project uses a testing pyramid: unit tests with Vitest (frontend) and Jest (backend), integration tests, and E2E tests with Playwright. MSW mocks API responses for frontend tests. The testing guides document what to test at each layer.

tour.title: Docker Infrastructure
tour.description: Docker Compose orchestrates the monorepo services: the NestJS API, PostgreSQL database, Mailpit email catcher, and Next.js frontend. Each service has its own Dockerfile with multi-stage builds for production optimization.
tour.languageLesson: Docker Compose uses YAML to define multi-service environments. The depends_on directive controls startup order. Named volumes persist database data across container restarts.

tour.title: Agent-Assisted Development
tour.description: The .claude directory contains a sophisticated AI-assisted development framework with custom skills, rules, and planning pipelines. This enables consistent code quality and architecture decisions across the development process.
